parsed.explanation: The traveller-facing record is mostly undocumented rather than adverse. No trans-specific criminal offence, border restriction, facility rule or custody practice is documented, and the sexuality statute was repealed in 1995. Against this, social disapproval is documented (56% want no public expression of homosexuality), parliamentarians have made hostile LGBT statements, and a 2016 constitutional removal occurred. Remedies exist (2013 hate-crime footing, reprimands) but are slow and inconsistently enforced. The ten violence cases lack a population denominator and are treated as undocumented. Legal gender recognition and document handling are unresolved, so entry-document exposure is an open question, weighted lightly. Overall: elevated, not reduced, risk.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented border refusal, questioning or document-mismatch treatment of trans visitors. Document marker handling is unresolved in the dossier.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor documents come from the home country; no operative local marker procedure is described that would touch them.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented police detention, custody placement or detention-based harm of trans people.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: No documented sovereign interaction path (border to custody) is recorded for trans visitors.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No documented facility-access or ward restriction by birth sex. Anti-discrimination law covers sexual orientation, sex characteristics and HIV; gender identity appears mainly through the 2013 hate-crime amendment.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Anti-discrimination law in force since 2010, with an operating commissioner who issued reprimands (2011), though slowly.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Commissioner oversight is functioning but slow, and its findings have not produced documented structural change.

care_services.exposure: A senior official publicly called homosexuality a hormonal and psychological disorder, and was reprimanded months later. No documented care denial to visitors.
care_services.protection: Health care is covered by anti-discrimination law (sexual orientation and HIV); no visitor-facing care protection is documented.
care_services.interaction: Official rhetoric about treatment creates a latent risk of discriminatory care; no operative denial is recorded.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Parliamentary and political framing of LGBT people as a 'suspicious, revolting agenda' and an imposed value. The 2013 dissemination offence carries up to two years, but no application is documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Reprimands for hostile statements; hate-crime law places gender identity motivation on par with other bias grounds.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State actors have voiced threat-framing; the dissemination offence is a latent speech constraint with no documented enforcement record.

minors_guardians.exposure: Opposition hostility to LGBT extracurricular groups in schools and a 2016 national action plan drew strong political opposition. No documented harm to a minor visitor.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor could encounter school-level friction; no documented school exclusion of visitors.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Ten bias-motivated violence cases against trans people logged by a community group in one year, with no population denominator, so they are undocumented as rate evidence.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime law covers gender identity; police response record is thin.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse for victims is slow; only one of nine LGBT-linked complaints had concluded by December 2012.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Complaints are slow, investigations are bureaucratically impeded, and advocacy groups have lost trust in the commissioner. Legal gender recognition is unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: UN expert visit (2024) and report (2025) give international scrutiny; the commissioner reprimanded officials.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists on paper and works only intermittently, so it does not reliably offset exposure.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A has a universal, state-run entry bar and exclusion of trans visitors with no effective remedy. This dossier documents no entry bar or exclusion, so it sits well above 0.35-A.

0.55-B has documented discretionary border secondary screening and denial of entry for trans visitors. This dossier has no documented border targeting, so it is at least similar to or slightly above 0.55-B on border exposure, though its remedies are weaker and its social hostility is documented.

0.75-C has documented respectful border practice and functioning remedies for detention. This dossier has no documented border protection and its remedies are slow and inconsistent, so it sits clearly below 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: No trans-specific criminal, border, facility or custody exposure is documented against visitors, and the sexuality statute has been repealed. The operative picture is documented societal disapproval, parliamentary and official hostile framing, a latent speech offence with no recorded use, and slow, unevenly enforced recourse. The hate-crime footing and reprimands are real but thin. Violence figures lack a denominator. Document and legal-recognition questions remain open and are weighted lightly. The result is elevated risk: no known tier-1 exposure, but enough threat-framing and remedy weakness to keep the rating below the reduced-risk band.
